newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Turkmens, Taleban mull return of Afghan refugees.
newsitem.headline: Turkmens, Taleban mull return of Afghan refugees.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban militia and Turkmen officials are considering the return of thousands of Afghan refugees who fled from heavy fighting to Turkmenistan, a senior Red Cross official said on Friday.

"Negotiations are going on between the Turkmen government and Afghanistan's Taleban over the return of the refugees," Bob McKerrow, head of a regional delegation of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), told Reuters in the Kazakh capital Almaty.
He gave no details of the negotiations.

McKerrow said 2,000-3,000 of about 8,000 people who fled to Turkmenistan last week to escape war in northern Afghanistan had already gone back across the border. Some had then wheeled around and gone to Turkmenistan again.
"There's still fighting in northern Afghanistan and refugees go home, but after one or two days at home they come back again," he said.

The refugees fled the town of Mari Chak on the Afghan side of the Murgab river, which separates the two countries, to escape fighting between Afghanistan's dominant Taleban militia and troops of Uzbek General Abdul Malik.
The Taleban are trying to regain control of territories in the north which they briefly won but then lost to the anti-Taleban alliance in May.
Refugees are in no-man's land in the desert on the Turkmen side of the Turkmen-Afghan border near the town of Takhta Bazar.

Thorir Gudmundsson, regional information delegate for the IFRC, said on Thursday that 13 refugees had died in Turkmenistan, mostly from diarrhoea. The death toll had risen to 14 by Friday after a child was bitted by a snake, he said.

The refugees at Takhta Bazar are the first major influx of displaced Afghans to any of the former Soviet Central Asian states, which had earlier voiced fears that fighting in Afghanistan could start an exodus of civilians.
